author: vladimir_ea
content: I have a couple of questions on this proposal: https://www.potuz.net/posts/gloas-circuit-breaker/

author: vladimir_ea
content:
- what is meant by missing payload? I am assuming that it means either not delivered but also includes delivered but invalid? 

the comment that most missing blocks are caused by large builder bugs suggests that this is the case, b/c currently missed slots can occur when the winning block is invalid (e.g. incorrect state root)

author: vladimir_ea
content: but i do not belive missed slots often occur becuase a large builder has failed to deliver the layload.

author: vladimir_ea
content: if ever

author: vladimir_ea
content:
"so that on a single failure we blacklist the builder for just one epoch, but on two consecutive failures during 5 epochs the builder is permanently banned until a restart"

if a 'single failure' includes invalid payloads (not just undelivered payload - which it must do to protect against DoS?) then this seems overly aggressive?

why is it assumed that a single invalid is a systemic error requiring a curcuit break? surely 2 consecutive invlaid blocks from the same builder would be more rationale circuit break? what do <@&1458826346896687229> think?

author: vladimir_ea
content: also I find the phrase "two consecutive failures during 5 epochs" somewhat confusing - what does it mean exactly?

author: ajsutton
content: There's really no excuse for building any bad block.

author: vladimir_ea
content: right, because all software is always perfect, no excuses.

author: vladimir_ea
content: back in the real world though, it does happen that invalid blocks win slots - this happens currently, albeit rarely, becuase none of the existing builders are actually perfect.  But these problems are in almost all cases transitory issues confined to a single slot.

author: vladimir_ea
content: so the question is whether it makes sense to ban a builder for an epoch following a single slot error?

author: ajsutton
content:
I don’t see why not. They have one job - to build valid blocks and they demonstrably have a bug. So better to avoid them and switch to something that’s not known to be defective. 
And having strong economic incentives in place for builders to ensure they don’t build bad blocks seems like a pretty good policy.

author: vladimir_ea
content: that seems to be a different rationale from having a circuit-breaker, as it seems unlikely that a bug will be fixed in the span of an epoch.

author: 0xunclebill
content: there is no room for client software to allow for attesting to bad blocks. there is no excuse for those type of error conditions. why cant we extend those requirements to block builders

author: 0xunclebill
content: builders should have their own internal circuit breakers that trigger as soon as they produce an invalid block

author: ajsutton
content: The circuit breaker minimises the damage to the network by switching to builders that are likely to work.

author: tersec
content: oh hey they used to then they did "optimistic validation" or something which practically has sometimes turned out to be "no validation because they gotta get out there 0.5ms quicker"

author: vladimir_ea
content: are there such builders? For example,  so far today all the major builders have submitted invalid blocks to Titan relay.

author: vladimir_ea
content: but also that this represents a very tiny percentage of all blocks submitted - 100ks of blocks are submitted per slot, and we get 1 or 2 invlaid per day.

author: vladimir_ea
content: relays implement circuit breakers - i don;t suppose builders do becauase currently they use relays

author: ajsutton
content:
I’m not really understanding the push back here. There are bad blocks - it’s better for the network if there were fewer of them. Making it hurt builders who produce invalid blocks more is a great way to incentivise more care. And the circuit breaker minimises the damage to the network. 
Builders who don’t want to be ignored for an epoch can just produce valid blocks which is entirely within their control. 
What’s the problem?

author: vladimir_ea
content:
> And the circuit breaker minimises the damage to the network. 
how does this 'ban single failure for an epoch' minimise damage to the network?

author: vladimir_ea
content: there are invalid blocks, they are extremely rare, what does blacklisting a builder for one-off rare events protect against?

author: vladimir_ea
content: if the there is a systemic problem with a builder then surely having 2 such events in some time interval would be a better way to protect?

author: ajsutton
content: Why not both? Again what’s the downside here? It’s better for the network and has strong economic alignment with the behaviour we want.

author: vladimir_ea
content:
well the downside of over zealous banning is you don't get the best value for proposers. 

if i understand then, this measure is not just a circuit-breaker but also intended as an economic incentive / penalty?

author: tersec
content: it aligns incentives. against _precisely_ this lack of care

author: tersec
content: builders don't want to care, so they must have to care

author: tersec
content: for the builders, it's a statistical game for the top builders

author: tersec
content: it's fine if an occasional block goes bad, it just doesn't really matter, and the cost of fixing it systemically appears to exceed the damage it does to their revenue
